transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I came in because I just can’t keep my mind on what I’m supposed to be doing anymore. At work, even in the middle of a grant call or a safety meeting, I’ll notice something like a pump vibration, or a student’s side comment, or some weird peak in an old spectrum, and then I’m gone — chasing that for hours. Meanwhile the actual experiment or the thing people needed from me just falls apart.
When you were a child, did you also have this kind of trouble staying focused on what you were supposed to be doing?

I don’t really remember it being like this as a child. What I’m dealing with now is more that I can’t keep my mind on the actual experiment or meeting. Like I said, I’ll be in a grant call or safety meeting and some little thing catches me — a pump vibration, a student’s comment, an odd peak in old data — and then I’m off chasing that for hours while the real thing falls apart.
Have you had times when your mood was unusually high or wired?

Yes. For months now I’ve felt like the lab is finally moving at my speed, like everything is kind of electrified. But if someone questions my plan or tells me to slow down, I snap at them. It’s gotten bad enough that some of the students avoid coming to my office.
Lately, have you been needing much less sleep than usual and still feeling fully energized?

Yes. Most nights I’m only sleeping maybe two or three hours. Sometimes I just pass out on the couch with my laptop still open, and then I wake up feeling sharp, like I’m ready to get back to work. I don’t really feel tired — it’s more like sleep is just getting in the way.
During this period, have you had experiences that other people would say were not real, like hearing voices or being certain of something that others said was impossible?
I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t been hearing voices or seeing things. I do feel very sure about my ideas sometimes, but I’m not sure that’s the same as something impossible.
Have you been convinced of something others said was impossible or clearly untrue?

Yes. I was completely convinced I could fix the whole multi-site project myself — redesign the spectroscopy approach, straighten out every student’s work better than their own advisors, and still make the grant deadline. It felt obvious to me that it would work if people would just stop slowing me down.
Even when other people showed you clear evidence that you could not do all of that yourself, were you still certain that you could?

Yes. Even when they showed me schedules or said there weren’t enough hours, I still felt sure I could do it. I honestly believed I could pull the whole project back on track myself if people would just get out of my way.
Have you been hospitalized because of this high-energy period?
I’m not sure how to answer that. I don’t have a hospitalization to tell you about from it, at least not that I’m aware of.
During this high-energy period, have you ever believed you had a special ability or power that other people said was not real?

Yes. I didn’t think of it like a supernatural power, but I did believe I had this special ability to fix everything myself. I was sure I could rescue the whole project, redo the spectroscopy plan, guide every student better than their advisors, and still beat the grant deadline if people would just stop getting in my way.
When other people clearly showed you that you could not do all of that yourself, did you still remain completely certain that you could?

Yes. Even when people laid it out for me and it was obvious to them it wasn’t possible, I still felt completely sure I could do it. I really believed I could save the whole project myself, redo the spectroscopy approach, mentor all the students better than their own advisors, and still make the grant deadline if everyone would just stop blocking me.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not sure. I don’t really have a clear two-week period like that in mind that I can point to.
Has this high-energy period caused serious problems in your life, like major trouble at work or with other people?

Yes, it has. My department had to step in on decisions I used to handle myself. I was missing priorities and mixing up scheduling, and the way I was supervising people got strained enough that it started putting the project and lab safety expectations at risk.
